en.headline: Customs seize HK$11 million of suspected controlled pharmaceuticals in Sheung Shui
en.dek: Officers raided a warehouse used for storage and repackaging, arresting two mainland two-way permit holders and seizing more than 400,000 items mostly for sexual health and cancer treatment.
body: Hong Kong Customs officers on Tuesday raided an industrial unit in Sheung Shui believed to be used for storing and repackaging suspected controlled pharmaceutical products, seizing more than 400,000 items with an estimated market value exceeding HK$11 million.

A 56-year-old woman who received the goods and a 51-year-old man working as a handyman, both holding mainland two-way permits, were arrested at the scene. More than 60 per cent of the seized products were for treating virility issues, with others including cancer treatment drugs. Packaging tools and large numbers of paper boxes were also found.

Customs said most of the products appeared to originate from South Asia and that none had entered the market. The Syndicate Crimes Investigation Bureau is continuing inquiries and has not ruled out further arrests. The Department of Health reminded the public not to buy or take medicines of unknown origin.

zh.headline: 海關上水搗破倉庫檢逾1100萬元受管制藥品拘兩人
zh.dek: 關員於上水工廈單位檢獲逾40萬件懷疑受管制藥劑製品，大部分為壯陽藥及抗癌藥，兩名雙程證持有人被捕。
body: 香港海關周二在上水一個工廈單位採取行動，搗破懷疑用作儲存及分裝受管制藥劑製品的倉庫，檢獲超過40萬件懷疑受管制藥劑製品，估計市值超過1100萬元。
一名56歲收件女子及一名51歲報稱雜工男子在場被捕，兩人均持有內地雙程證。檢獲產品中超過六成為壯陽藥，其餘包括抗癌藥等。單位內亦發現大量紙皮箱、膠紙等包裝工具。
海關表示，大部分產品相信來自南亞，目前並無流出市面。有組織罪案調查科繼續調查，不排除再有人被捕。衞生署提醒市民切勿購買或服用來歷不明的藥物。
